text:
maria: Heads-up — overnight we had a ~15min wave of preemptible GPU evictions in us-west1, multiple jobs raced to fallback and caused a short capacity crunch. Not panicking but want to align on mitigations.
kevin: saw it in pager duty. Which nodepools got hit? any pattern by machine type?
maria: mostly g4dn-like preemptible pool (gpu-preemptible-usw1). Eviction events clustered across 3 AZs around 03:10 UTC. Autoscaler scaled up ok but draining + pod startup lagged.
ada: ada here — quick thought: our rotation/orchestration waits for nodeReady + kubelet sync before reassigning heavy jobs; that adds ~30-45s per pod. Can we parallelize or use fast-swap for queued batches?
maria: yes. Proposal: 1) enable faster pod eviction for batch GPUs with gracePeriod 15s for these workloads; 2) keep a tiny on-demand shadow pool (2-3 nodes) with taint:reserved=preemptions:NoSchedule and matching tolerations for critical pods; 3) reduce node auto-provisioner scale step delay from 60s -> 20s for this pool only.
kevin: +1 for shadow pool, but cost question — rough delta?
ben: back-of-envelope: 3 p4-equivalent hours x 24 x 30 ~ +$Xk/mo depending on commit discounts. Worth it for customer SLAs. We can gate via workload label so only high-priority jobs land there.
ada: PR for kube configs would be small. Example drain command we use in tests:
```
kubectl drain node-abc --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=15 --force
```
maria: also want to try staggered rotation: instead of draining all evicted nodes immediately, rotate a small fraction to on-demand while letting rest reprovision from preemptible pool. That reduced thrash in the sim.
ops-bot: ALERT: Preemptible-eviction-wave detected in cluster=prod-us-west1 @ 2026-03-16T03:10:12Z (evictions: 42, nodes lost: 7)
kevin: can we run the shadow-pool in us-west1 only to avoid cross-region latency?
ben: yes, keep it regional. Also recommend using nodeAffinity anti-affinity to spread these fallback nodes across AZs so we don't lose all at once.
ada: I'll draft the PR for autoscaler tuning + taint/toleration + new nodepool spec. Want to run a canary in staging (europe-west1) first.
maria: perfect. Who can own rollout? kevin?
kevin: I can own rollout and monitor latency & token-cost metrics. Will run the canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC.
ben: I'll run cost sim and report expected monthly delta.
maria: thanks — add the rollout checklist to the PR: metrics to watch = pod start latency, queued work, eviction count, CPU/GPU utilisation, on-demand spend. If canary looks good we'll flip on for prod-us-west1 next week. :thumbsup:
kevin: noted. Also adding an alert to detect shadow-pool saturation so it doesn't get overwhelmed.
ada: PR draft in ~2h, ping me if you want to test the drain script locally.
ops-bot: NOTE: Deploy-bot scheduled maintenance for autoscaler at 2026-03-17T12:00:00Z (window 30m)
